themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks (256% increase, z-score: 3.68), signaling a rapid escalation in Uber/Lyft-related disturbances or street obstruction in Mott Haven/Melrose this week.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Suggests new problem or sudden intensification of existing gig-vehicle issues
reporting_angles: Interview residents about illegal drop-offs, double parking, or congestion caused by Uber/Lyft vehicles in residential blocks
Check with TLC and 311 data to confirm whether spike is localized to Mott Haven or citywide; if localized, investigate why (new transit hub, reduced enforcement, or driver behavior change)

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Persist
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints reached 3 this week—a 367% increase over the 0.8 weekly baseline—and represent a sustained 4-week trend, indicating ongoing community friction with illicit or unlicensed cannabis operations in the district.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Sustained elevation for 4 weeks indicates systemic issue, not one-off incident
reporting_angles: Map which blocks have the most complaints; investigate whether illegal storefronts are clustering in specific corridors (e.g., Grand Concourse, 3rd Ave)
Interview community board, local precinct, and neighbors about enforcement gaps; confirm whether complaints are about odor, loitering, or unlicensed vs. licensed retailers

themes_detail.label: Park Safety & Rule Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violations of park rules exploded to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago (2300% above the 0.1 weekly baseline) and park noise spiked to 4 complaints 2 weeks ago (540% above baseline), with sustained momentum (2 park noise complaints this week), suggesting deteriorating conditions or new activities in Mott Haven/Melrose parks.
evidence: Park rule violations: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Park noise: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Sustained concern: 2 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (260% spike, z-score: 2.33)
reporting_angles: Visit parks in the district (Crotona Park, St. Mary's Park) to observe what rule violations or noise sources are driving complaints—unauthorized events, late-night gatherings, vendors, loitering?
Interview Parks Dept., local precinct, and community members about whether recent policy changes, staffing reductions, or new activities have degraded park conditions

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 12 last week, up 160% from the 4.6 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.69), reflecting a recent surge in disturbances from businesses, restaurants, or street vendors in the district.
evidence: 12 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing suggests new commercial activity, expanded hours, or venue openings in the district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with recent DoE liquor license approvals or new restaurant openings in Mott Haven/Melrose
Interview neighbors about which specific businesses or blocks are generating noise; determine whether complaints are about music, outdoor service, delivery trucks, or construction-related

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints more than doubled to 10 last week, a 135% increase over the 4.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 2.9), signaling a recent uptick in resident concerns about crime, unsafe conditions, or emergency incidents in the district.
evidence: 10 safety complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
311 data does not specify nature of safety concerns (crime, hazards, accidents); requires follow-up reporting
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 complaint texts to categorize safety concerns (assault, robbery, hazardous conditions, traffic danger, etc.)
Cross-reference with NYPD incident reports and local precinct (44th or 41st) to confirm whether reported crimes align with resident complaints
